ledger.note: 1454: Amir bin Tahir takes the title of sultan and the Tahirids succeed the Rasulids in the Tihama and the southern highlands. Infobox 'Established: 1454', 'They succeeded the Rasulid Dynasty'; 'The eldest of the brothers, Amir bin Tahir, took the titles sultan and king'; the family 'were trustees of the sultans of the Rasulid dynasty' and 'ruled in the first place in the Tihama lowland and the southern highlands'. Lahij, their clan's gain, was 'taken over by them in 1443', eleven years before the state (the Rasulid dossier has the 1443 loss). The page names no boundary and does not date Zabid or the highlands coming under them, so the region is the researcher's reading.

1454: the brothers Amir and Ali bin Tahir take Aden. 'in 1454, the important port of Aden was swiftly taken by the brothers Amir and Ali bin Tahir'; the last Rasulid sultan 'withdrew to Mecca in the same year'. The page gives no month.

zones.text: San'a and the highlands round it

wars.outcome: The Tahirid army sent against the imam al-Mutawakkil al-Mutahhar was defeated in 1458; San'a was entered temporarily in 1461; the old sultan Amir was killed fighting the Zaydis in 1466; Amir II took San'a again in 1504. The Zaydi imams 'were mostly able to resist Tahirid rule'.
wars.note: A descriptive name, not a Wikipedia title. The page gives four dated incidents and no continuous war; the ledger contests San'a only 1461-1466 and the gain is 1504.

wars.name: Mamluk conquest of Yemen

zones.text: 'The entire Tahirid realm' (Tihama, the southern highlands and Sana'a) 'with the exception of Aden which held out under the Tahirid governor Amir Murjan'

wars.outcome: The second Mamluk fleet under Husain al-Kurdi, equipped in 1515, took the Tahirid treasure house at al-Miqranah, beheaded Sultan Amir II near San'a on 15 May and overran the whole realm except Aden; the fleet withdrew after setting up a tributary regime in Zabid.

wars.name: Siege of Aden (1513)
wars.outcome: The Portuguese attack on Aden was beaten off by the Tahirids; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The page's sentence says only that Husain al-Kurdi found the Tahirids having 'recently beaten off a Portuguese attack on Aden'; the year 1513 is read from the title of the article the sentence links to, not from the sentence itself.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier line. The northern limit against the Zaydi highlands, the Hadramawt coast and the extent of the Tihama are approximate; Aden and Sana'a are points with a radius, not borders.

notes:
Page budget was 1-2 (2 Cliopatria shapes); three pages were opened because the first, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tahirid_dynasty (Cliopatria's Wikipedia field for this row), is the Persian Tahirids of Khorasan (821-873), not the Yemeni state; the right article is 'Tahirid Sultanate' (identity.wikipedia is set to it, polities.csv should be corrected). The third page (Amir Husain Al-Kurdi) was silent on Yemen.

Cliopatria rows: the two shapes (1459-1511, 1512-1515) are identical and identical to the Rasulid Dynasty rows (377,949.8 km2, 1,633 cells). They reach Sa'dah, al-Jawf, Ma'rib, Shabwah, the Hadramawt interior, al-Mahrah and about 200 Saudi cells; the page supports only 'the Tihama lowland and the southern highlands', Aden and Lahij, Shihr (1457 to about 1499) and Sana'a (1504 on). All shapes are therefore verdict adjust with a region correction of about 115,000-124,000 km2. The Rasulid dossier (me-09-d) kept the same outline as fitting its page (coast 'up to Dhofar'); a reviewer should decide whether the Tahirid outline should follow it. The mamluk-sultanate dossier's 1516 gain draws on Cliopatria's Tahirid 1515 shape (1,633 cells), far larger than the corrected realm; it should reference this dossier's 1516 keyframe instead.

Dates: Cliopatria 1459-1515; the page 1454-1517 (infobox 'Established: 1454', 'Disestablished: 1517'). The mamluk-sultanate dossier has the Yemen gain in 1516 (confidence 1, bridged from Cliopatria); this dossier has the realm falling in 1517 (the page's year; the 15 May of the sultan's death carries no year on the page) and the contest opening in 1515 (the second fleet, confidence 1). The page does not date the landing, Zabid, Ta'izz or Sana'a falling.

Not settled: (1) Aden: 'held out under the Tahirid governor Amir Murjan' in 1517 and the reign table carries sultans to 1538 (Amir bin Da'ud, 'cornered at Aden', executed 3 August 1538); this dossier ends in 1517 and does not draw an Aden remnant for 1517-1538; if the reviewer wants one it is Aden with a 25 km radius, successor ottoman-empire in 1538. (2) The 1443 Lahij gain precedes the state and is not a ledger event (the Rasulid dossier has the 1443 loss without a mirror); Lahij is in the 1454 founding region. (3) 1461: the page's 'The latter was able to enter San'a temporarily' does not say who 'the latter' is. (4) Who held Shihr before 1457 and when the Kathiri took it ('end of the fifteenth century'; 1499 bridged). (5) Zabid, Ta'izz, al-Janad, Ibb, Dhamar: no dates or conquests on the page; Dhamar and Abyan are the researcher's reading of 'southern highlands'. (6) Hadramawt beyond Shihr, Kamaran, Dhofar and the 1505-1509 Mamluk fleet (the Tahirids supplied it; no territorial effect) are not described. (7) The Zaydi imams of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries have no dossier: the slug imamate-of-yemen is used as in the Rasulid dossier, though Cliopatria's row covers 1814-1872. (8) The Kathiri (slug kathiri-sultanate, as in the Rasulid dossier) has none yet.

Gazetteer: Juban and al-Miqranah (the summer residences, about 80 km south of Rada'a), Rada'a and Dhu Marmar are not in the gazetteer; none is used in a region spec. 'Ash Shihr', 'Sanaa', 'Aden', the admin-1 names Ta`izz, Ibb, Dhamar, Al Bayda', Lahij, Al Dali', Abyan and `Adan, and the region 'Tihama' resolve. The corrected radii (Shihr 60 km, Sana'a 50 km, Aden 25 km) are the researcher's. Native names are added by the researcher, not from the page.
